answer_1.quote: In this study, we address the challenge of minimizing misgendering across 42 languages and dialects within an AI-based application... in a meeting transcript summarization context.
answer_1.outputs: summaries of meeting transcripts in multiple languages with reduced misgendering

answer_2.quote: We establish two metrics to identify instances of misgendering, along with one quality metric to assess whether the language-specific guardrails adversely impact the output quality.

answer_3.quote: We use both LLM-and human-based evaluation techniques to test the efficacy of our guardrails... we use GPT-4o, Phi-3.5-MoE-Instruct and Qwen-25-vl7b as judges.

answer_4.quote: The human evaluation was done by three native speakers per language. They were requested to evaluate the model's output with the same metrics (GM, GA, Q) from Section 4.3.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluate the model's output with the same metrics: Gender Mistake (GM), Gender Assumption (GA), and Quality (Q). A high-quality summary includes all key points, identifies participants, and is grammatically correct and fluent.
